At a glance

Best months
May for the Seewinkel and the eastern steppe, late June and July for the Alpine road, and February to April for the woodpeckers and the Ural Owls
Getting around
Austria is the easiest country on this site to bird by train. Rail reaches the Seewinkel, the Wienerwald and the Gesause, and cable cars reach the high ground. The Grossglockner road wants a car
The one thing to know
The Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse closes for the winter and late snow can delay the reopening, so an Alpine trip is planned around the road rather than the other way round

When to Go

The Austrian year splits cleanly in two. The eastern lowlands run from late winter through spring, with the woodpeckers drumming before the bustards display, and the mountains only start once the high road opens.

spring

March to May

The lowland season. Great Bustards display on the Parndorf Plain, the Seewinkel soda pans fill with breeding waders and the forests are drumming.

Go for Great Bustard, Saker Falcon, the breeding waders and the woodpecker set.

Trade off The Alpine passes are still shut, so the mountain list is out of reach until late spring.

Typical daily average Wien 6 to 15 °C / 43 to 59 °F, Innsbruck 4 to 15 °C / 39 to 59 °F, Bregenz 4 to 12 °C / 39 to 54 °F

summer

June to August

The Alpine season. The Grossglockner road is open and the high ground holds Lammergeier, Alpine Accentor, Snowfinch and Ptarmigan.

Go for The full Alpine list, Red-footed Falcon in the Seewinkel, Spoonbill on the pans.

Trade off The soda pans dry through summer and the Alpine roads carry heavy tourist traffic.

Typical daily average Wien 14 to 25 °C / 57 to 77 °F, Innsbruck 12 to 23 °C / 54 to 73 °F, Bregenz 12 to 21 °C / 54 to 70 °F

autumn

September to October

Passage through the Rheindelta and the eastern wetlands, with the first wildfowl arriving on Lake Constance.

Go for Wader and wildfowl passage, raptors moving south.

Trade off The Grossglockner road closes for the winter, usually from late autumn.

Typical daily average Wien 8 to 17 °C / 46 to 63 °F, Innsbruck 6 to 18 °C / 43 to 64 °F, Bregenz 8 to 16 °C / 46 to 61 °F

winter

November to February

Lake Constance and the Danube hold the wintering waterbirds, and late winter starts the woodpeckers drumming and the Ural Owls calling.

Go for Wintering waterbirds, White-tailed Eagle, and the first forest song of the year.

Trade off The Alps are closed to birding and the eastern lakes can freeze.

Typical daily average Wien -1 to 5 °C / 30 to 41 °F, Innsbruck -2 to 6 °C / 28 to 43 °F, Bregenz -2 to 4 °C / 28 to 39 °F

A Vienna Layover

The Seewinkel in Spring

Vienna (VIE), Illmitz, the soda pans, the Parndorf Plain

An hour southeast of Vienna and everything within a short drive of Illmitz. May takes the breeding waders, the falcons and the bustards together.

The Alpine Road

Salzburg (SZG), Mittersill, the Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse, Mallnitz

The high road is the trip. Check it is open before booking, because it closes for the winter and can shut in late snow.

Forests and Woodpeckers

Linz (LNZ), the Kalkalpen, the Gesause, the Wienerwald

Late winter into early spring, when the woodpeckers are drumming and the Ural Owls are calling. The Kalkalpen core zone is the set piece.

13 days

Austria End to End

Vienna (VIE), the Seewinkel, Marchegg, the Wienerwald, the Kalkalpen, the Gesause, the Hohe Tauern, the Tyrol, the Rheindelta

East to west, lowland steppe to Alpine road to Lake Constance. Late May into June is the window when the passes are open and the lowlands are still breeding.

Neusiedler See, the Seewinkel and the Parndorf Plain

The reason most birders come to Austria. Neusiedler See is a shallow steppe lake with a reed belt kilometres wide, and the Seewinkel behind it is a scatter of soda pans that hold Avocet, Spoonbill, Red-footed Falcon and Black-tailed Godwit. The Parndorf Plain above carries Great Bustard and Saker Falcon.

Where to Stay6 places to stay

Austria is the third country in a row where the obvious scheme is the wrong one. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, and leading on it would produce a near-empty section. What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Every property below carries a certification from a scheme's own record and sits within reach of somewhere this guide sends you. What each certification actually means

The March Floodplains and Marchegg

Marchegg holds the largest tree-nesting White Stork colony in Europe, in oak floodplain forest on the March river. The floodplain behind gives Black Stork, White-tailed Eagle and the woodpeckers, and it is forty minutes from Vienna.

The Danube Wetlands and Donau-Auen

The Danube east of Vienna runs through the last free-flowing floodplain forest on its Austrian length, protected as a national park. The wetlands here are side-arms, gravel banks and softwood forest, with Kingfisher, Black Woodpecker, White-tailed Eagle and a beaver population.

Also covers: Coburgbastei, Kärntner Strasse, Parkring, Petersplatz, Ringstrasse, Schottenring, Schubertring, Staatsoper, Vienna

Where to Stay156 places to stay

Austria is the third country in a row where the obvious scheme is the wrong one. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, and leading on it would produce a near-empty section. What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Every property below carries a certification from a scheme's own record and sits within reach of somewhere this guide sends you. What each certification actually means

Austria is the third country in a row where the obvious scheme is the wrong one. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, and leading on it would produce a near-empty section. What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Hohe Tauern and the Grossglockner

The Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse climbs to two and a half thousand metres and is the single best Alpine birding road in the country. Lammergeier, Golden Eagle, Alpine Accentor, Snowfinch, Ptarmigan and Alpine Chough, with national park centres at Mittersill, Mallnitz and Matrei.

What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Every property below carries a certification from a scheme's own record and sits within reach of somewhere this guide sends you. What each certification actually means

Tyrol, the Zugspitze-Wetterstein and Karwendel

The Tyrolean limestone around Ehrwald, under the Zugspitze and the Wetterstein wall. The cable car gives the high ground quickly, Alpine Accentor and Wallcreeper on the rock, and the Karwendel behind holds the same set with a longer walk in.

Look for:

Also covers: A- Grins, A- Nesselwängle Nr. 71, A- Pians, A- Schattwald, Grän, Innsbruck, Inntal, Längenfeld, Leutasch, Mieming, Neustift im Stubaital, Niederthai, Obsteig, Pettneu am Arlberg, Pitztal, Seefeld, Telfs, Umhausen, Zöblen

Where to Stay47 places to stay

Austria is the third country in a row where the obvious scheme is the wrong one. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, and leading on it would produce a near-empty section. What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Every property below carries a certification from a scheme's own record and sits within reach of somewhere this guide sends you. What each certification actually means

The Rheindelta and Vorarlberg's Lake Constance Shore

Austria is the third country in a row where the obvious scheme is the wrong one. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, and leading on it would produce a near-empty section. What carries the country is the Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, Austria's own national ecolabel, whose tourism register lists on the order of six hundred establishments across all nine states. That figure is a count taken off the register's own listing rather than an official published total, and it is stated that way on purpose. Kalkalpen and the Reichraminger Hintergebirge

The Kalkalpen national park protects the largest unbroken forest wilderness in Austria, and the Reichraminger Hintergebirge core zone is the reason it holds all the woodpeckers, White-backed among them. Sengsengebirge above adds the mountain birds.

Mr & Mrs Smithi-escape

The ebb of the seasons sets the agenda at Refugium Lunz, a hygge-infused basecamp amid Lower Austria’s wild alpine landscape. Winter days spent skiing are thawed with stints in the mountain-gazing sauna, while warmer months bring crystalline lake swims and hikes through wildflower meadows. And then there are the perennial pleasures: exquisite regional cuisine, fresh-baked cakes to help yourself to, and a crisp riesling on the terrace as the river lazes past below.

Birding Community

Birding here runs through a BirdLife partner and six national parks, and the parks manage most of the ground this page sends you to. Find a birding organisation near you in our worldwide directory

Alongside the national bodies below, Austria has 8 local bird clubs across 9 regions. They run the walks and the counts, and most of them welcome visitors. See every Austrian club by region.

BirdLife Österreich The BirdLife partner in Austria, running the rarities committee, the monitoring schemes and the conservation work on the eastern steppe. Visit Nationalpark Neusiedler See-Seewinkel Manages the soda pans and the reed belt, and runs the Illmitz centre that most visits start from. Visit Nationalpark Hohe Tauern The largest national park in the Alps, with visitor centres at Mittersill, Mallnitz and Matrei, and the Lammergeier work. Visit Nationalpark Kalkalpen Protects the largest unbroken forest wilderness in Austria, which is why the full woodpecker set survives there. Visit

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the best time to go birding in Austria?

May for the lowlands and late June for the Alps, which is why a trip covering both usually runs in early June. The Seewinkel is at its best in May and the Grossglockner road needs the passes open.

Where do I go for Great Bustard in Austria?

The Parndorf Plain above the Seewinkel, and the Hansag on the Hungarian border. The birds are on farmland managed for them and are watched from the road at range, because they are protected from disturbance.

Is the Grossglockner road open all year?

No. It closes for the winter and reopens in late spring, and late snow can delay that. Check the road's own site before booking an Alpine trip around it, because there is no alternative at that height.

Which country is best for woodpeckers in Europe?

Austria has a strong claim. The Kalkalpen national park holds the largest unbroken forest wilderness in the country, and its Reichraminger Hintergebirge core zone carries the dead-wood specialists including White-backed.

Can I bird Austria without a car?

More than most countries, yes. The rail network reaches Illmitz for the Seewinkel, the Wienerwald and the Gesause, and cable cars take you onto the high ground at Rax and Ehrwald. The Grossglockner road still wants a car.

What certification should I look for in Austrian accommodation?

The Österreichisches Umweltzeichen, the Austrian Ecolabel, which is the national scheme and carries the tourism sector here. Green Key has almost no Austrian presence, so it is the wrong thing to look for.

What is the Ural Owl doing in Austria?

It was reintroduced after most of a century's absence, into the Wienerwald biosphere park and the wilderness area south of Vienna, and it now breeds. Late winter is when the birds call.

Who are the birding institutions in Austria?

BirdLife Österreich is the partner organisation and runs the rarities committee and the monitoring. The national parks at Neusiedler See, Hohe Tauern, Donau-Auen, Kalkalpen, Thayatal and Gesäuse manage most of the ground on this page.
